transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-02 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Emily Chen (Oxbridge Head of Security), Raj Patel (Oxbridge CTO), Maya Singh (Oxbridge Platform Engineer)

Auto sections (optional):
Summary: See metadata summary above.
Topics: SOC2/ISO proof, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS options (customer-managed), hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, timelines.
Action items (captured): see metadata action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Samira from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Diego from our engineering team is here too. How's everyone?
[00:10] Emily (Oxbridge): Hi, yeah thanks. I'm Emily, head of security at Oxbridge. We run retail inventory and personalization stuff, so data sensitivity is a big topic for us.
[00:15] Raj (CTO): Raj here. We're evaluating options — want to understand security posture and whether we can bring our own KMS and run in our VPC.
[00:22] Diego (SE): Great, thanks. Quick agenda — run through compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO), auth (SSO/SAML), access controls (RBAC), audit logging & retention, and KMS/encryption. Then tradeoffs for hosted/dedicated/private and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:32] Emily: Yep.
[00:34] Maya (Platform Eng): Works for me.
[00:36] Samira: Perfect. Quick question to set context — are you currently SOC2 Type II certified or in progress?
[00:42] Emily: We're SOC2 in-scope, our current vendor stack is working toward Type II but we have SOC2 for some parts. We need Redwood to provide SOC2 evidence for hosted offerings or we need a private deployment.
[00:52] Raj: To add — our legal team will need the reports. If Redwood hosted can't provide SOC2 attestation covering data plane, we'll probably push for Dedicated with contractual controls, or Private.
[01:03] Diego: Understood. Briefly: our hosted API is backed by Redwood's SOC2 coverage — we'll share the attestation. For Dedicated and Private, you get additional isolation and contractual SLAs. For Private we can deploy a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:18] Emily: When you say "share attestation" — is it redactable? We often need redacted versions for sensitive ops.
[01:22] Samira: Yes, we provide a SOC2 summary and a redactable report for security/partners. We'll attach the cert and the summary doc.
[01:28] Maya: On KMS — our requirement is that customer-managed keys are used for all persistent model artifacts and logs. Can Redwood integrate with AWS KMS or an HSM?
[01:37] Diego: Yes — we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we currently offer envelope encryption with our managed keys, but we have a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) roadmap for customers at Enterprise tier. That roadmap is in progress.
[01:52] Raj: Roadmap is fine, but we need a timeline. Our compliance team will not sign off without BYOK for logs and model weights at rest.
[01:59] Samira: Noted. Diego, can you outline the current technical constraints and what we can do now?
[02:03] Diego: Sure. For Dedicated we can attach a customer KMS via IAM role to the cluster — basically the inference nodes encrypt model artifacts with your KMS. Audit logs can be pushed to your S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS keys. For Private deployments we can place the entire control plane inside your VPC and integrate directly with your HSM. For hosted, until BYOK is GA, we can support encryption in transit and our managed at-rest keys, plus contractual obligations and limited redaction.
[02:32] Emily: Ok. About SSO — we use Okta and SAML for admin access. Do you support SAML-based SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[02:42] Samira: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync across Redwood Console for both Hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments, you can self-host the auth connector.
[02:52] Maya: Do you have fine-grained RBAC? We don't want engineers to have admin-level ability to change key rotation or data-retention policies.
[02:59] Diego: We do — role-based access with least-privilege. You can create roles scoped to projects and models. There are admin roles, model-deploy roles, and observability/readonly roles. We also have token scopes for API keys so you can restrict per-route/model access.
[03:15] Raj: How audited is the RBAC? We need audit trails that capture who requested model rollouts and who downloaded embeddings.
[03:22] Diego: All actions in the Redwood Console and API calls are logged. For Dedicated/Private, logs are streamed to your logging endpoint or S3 with timestamps and request IDs. We keep a default 90-day retention but retention windows are configurable per contract.
[03:37] Emily: Retention is key — our policy: logs must be retained for 1 year for some flows, and we have data residency requirements — some logs must not leave EU. Can Redwood's logging pipeline be region-restricted?
[03:48] Samira: Yes, region restriction is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has regionalized endpoints but please detail which artifacts must stay in-region and we'll map options.
[03:58] Maya: Quick clarification — are the model KV caches considered persistent data? We want assurance that cached prompts are ephemeral and not stored with PII.
[04:07] Diego: KV cache is ephemeral in memory during inference. We do have optional prefix caching for throughput; that can be disabled or configured to only cache non-sensitive payloads. Persistent artifacts are model weights, fine-tune artifacts, and logs. We treat prompt inputs as request data per our retention policy and can configure retention or deletion hooks.
[04:31] Emily: Useful. On data deletion — we need an API to purge data and a contractual SLA for deletion. Is that available?
[04:39] Samira: Yes — we support data deletion requests. For Hosted we provide deletion endpoints and confirm deletion in logs; Dedicated/Private gives you full control with your own storage. We'll include the deletion workflow in the documentation we send.
[04:52] Raj: Any third-party subprocessors for hosted? We need a list for vendor review.
[04:58] Samira: We'll attach a subprocessors list. For Hosted we do use cloud providers for compute and a CDN for content, listed in the doc. For Dedicated, you can select the cloud region and control providers.
[05:10] Maya: Encryption in transit — TLS versions?
[05:13] Diego: TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 supported on endpoints. Mutual TLS is available for certain dedicated endpoints if you require mTLS between services.
[05:22] Emily: For identity & access: do API keys support per-model scoping and expiry? We want short-lived keys and rotation automation.
[05:30] Diego: Yes, API tokens support scopes and TTLs. We also integrate with your Vault or can rotate keys via SCIM. 
[05:38] Raj: From a procurement lens — pricing for Dedicated vs Private — do you have a TCO calc?
[05:44] Samira: We do. We'll send a TCO spreadsheet showing baseline cost differences and breakouts: GPUs, instance hours, support, and licensing. For Dedicated we offer reserved capacity and burst options. Private includes a platform fee.
[05:57] Emily: One concern — latency. Our use-case is customer-facing personalization, so 50–100ms p95 is target. What options get us there?
[06:07] Diego: For sub-100ms p95, an edge-proxied Dedicated deployment in the same cloud region plus continuous batching tuned for your sequence lengths works well. Hosted can be fast too, depending on region and model size. We'll propose performance configurations and run a benchmark pilot.
[06:21] Maya: Benchmarks — can we run sample payloads?
[06:24] Diego: Yes, Diego: we can run a 1-week pilot with a small dedicated pool and your representative prompt set to show p95 and token costs.
[06:34] Raj: Timeline — we need compliance sign-off by end of June. Realistic?
[06:40] Samira: If we start pilot next week, provide your infra diagram and requirements, we can aim for a Dedicated pilot and deliver SOC2 docs and KMS integration plan in 4–6 weeks.
[06:50] Emily: Good. A few detailed questions from our security checklist: 1) Do you have TLS termination locations? 2) How are service account keys stored? 3) Do you have penetration testing cadence and results?
[07:02] Diego: 1) TLS terminates at the service front end; we have edge termination in region and mTLS for private endpoints. 2) Service account keys are stored in a secrets store with HSM-backed KMS; for Dedicated/Private you can configure your own KMS. 3) We do quarterly pentests and we'll share summaries and remediation notes — redacted reports as needed.
[07:22] Emily: For RBAC, can you show an example policy where a service account only has read metrics but not write or export access?
[07:29] Diego: We can — we'll attach sample RBAC policies and token scopes.
[07:33] Maya: Regarding audit logs structure — is there a canonical export format (e.g., JSON with request id, user id, action, timestamp)?
[07:41] Diego: Yes, logs are structured JSON with request_id, user_id, action, resource, timestamp, and outcome. They can be exported as ndjson to S3 or streamed to Splunk/Datadog.
[07:53] Emily: Residency — we need EU-only storage for some PII. Can Dedicated ensure no cross-border replication?
[07:59] Samira: Yes, Dedicated and Private support regionally pinned storage and we can contractually guarantee no cross-region replication for certain artifacts. 
[08:08] Raj: Ok. Switching to a slightly different angle — do you offer SOC2 + ISO artifacts as part of enterprise contract or only hosted?
[08:15] Samira: We include SOC2 attestation for Redwood-hosted. For Dedicated/Private we include contractual clauses and can provide attestation scoped to the managed control plane; Private lets you own more of the evidence.
[08:27] Emily: Our lawyers will want indemnities and data processing addendum details.
[08:31] Samira: We'll send a copy of our DPA and standard contract language. Legal can do redlines once they see it.
[08:36] Raj: Are there any platform-level guardrails to prevent model exfiltration?
[08:41] Diego: We have built-in rate-limiting, output filters, and optionally redaction at the prefix level. For high-security deployments we recommend private/air-gapped and additional network controls.
[08:54] Maya: One small text-parsing question — sometimes autop transcripts show 'K-V cash' — that's the KV cache, right?
[08:58] Samira: Yeah, common transcription issue — KV cache, not K-V cash.
[09:02] [laughter]
[09:05] Emily: Alright, let's capture the explicit next steps and who owns them.
[09:09] Samira: I'll recap. Samira to send SOC2 attestation, ISO summary, subprocessors list, and redactable report. Diego to send RBAC examples, log schema, and Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark sheet. Maya to share VPC diagram and list of compliance controls. We'll schedule a Diego-led infra walkthrough week of 5/11.
[09:29] Raj: Sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood side for BYOK timeline?
[09:33] Diego: For BYOK in Hosted, GA timeline is TBD; we can offer Dedicated with immediate KMS integration. We'll mark BYOK as a priority for your account.
[09:43] Emily: For our procurement, can you send pricing tiers for Reserved Dedicated capacity and an estimate for a small pilot?
[09:50] Samira: Yes — TCO & pilot pricing included in next email.
[09:54] Maya: For audit logs retention — can we get a sample retention config manifest?
[09:58] Diego: We'll attach a sample retention policy file that maps log types to retention days and residency.
[10:06] Samira: Great. Any last questions?
[10:09] Emily: Not right now.
[10:10] Raj: All good.
[10:12] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite for the infra walkthrough.
[10:18] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quality: some proper nouns were fuzzy (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed oddly as 'K-V cash', 'BYOK' sometimes 'B Y O K' split). There is occasional crosstalk and truncated sentences typical of remote calls.
